_readme: The improv stage, its story scene cards and the director's notes.

set: one stage for every story. 'places' are the only places an action may name, and the game turns any other name into 'looks around'. The places stand in for whatever a story needs, and each card's premise says what the Riser plays. The 'what' text of a place is public, like the rest of the set and the card. Keep the names short: the input LLM and the robots' actions (T19) use them.

cards: each one is a comedy version of a famous story. A card's 'seats' are dealt in random order to the actors on stage at Scene Prep, and a card has 5 seats, one for each actor in a full show, and a scene with fewer actors on stage uses fewer of them. Every want must work when any one or two seats are left out. 'backdrop' is the scene's painted backdrop flat (T17): an id and one line that describes it. 'props' is the four props the card brings to the Prop Table. A want names only its own card's props and the places, and at least one prop, the spare, is named by no want, so the card still works if the spare is dropped. The game sends actors only the card's title and premise, plus each seat's role and want, and the card's props as the state's set.props (T45). Each seat's 'headpiece' (an id in costumes.json) and 'color' (sRGB hex) dress the robot that plays it (T47); the game never sends them to the AIs.

Story rules: public-domain stories (Shakespeare, fairy tales, classic novels) can stay close to the original. Modern films and books are parodied only: new names, no trademarked terms or made-up words from them, no quotes, no logos. No real people's names. Tools/check_prompts.py lists the words from each modern original that must never show up, in the files or in a reply.

notes: each scene draws one note, and every AI actor gets it; the human's seat gets none (T50). The human's card shows a clue to it instead, a different kind each scene (T88, clues.json). Its 'category' (Movement, Props, Looks or Speech) says what kind of thing the note is about and never what to do; it is scene 1's clue. The other fields feed the other kinds: 'key' is one word of the note, written as it is there; 'emoji' is 2 to 4 emoji; 'opposite' is the reverse rule, no longer than the note; 'riddle' is at most 10 words in the director's voice, without the key word; 'autocorrect' is the note with two or three words changed to near-spellings. A note applies during the scene's 3 turns. Notes are mostly physical, so the log shows who follows them, and each one must work in every story, with any card's four props. Notes never ask everyone to grab the same single prop.

places.name: Center
places.what: the middle of the stage, under the main spotlight

places.name: Front
places.what: the front edge of the stage, by the footlights and the audience

places.name: Back
places.what: the back of the stage, in front of the painted backdrop

places.name: Riser
places.what: a sturdy wooden box that plays whatever the story needs: a balcony, a throne, a cockpit, a lookout tower

places.name: Prop Table
places.what: the table at the side of the stage that holds the props

cards.title: Who Hid the Plans in the Robot?
cards.premise: Planet Dust, a desert world with two suns. A rebel hid the stolen plans to a moon-sized battle station inside a tin-can robot, and a masked villain who breathes very loudly is coming to get them back. The Riser is the cockpit of a battered space truck.

backdrop.what: A desert at dusk under two suns, with a rusty dome hut, a battered space truck and a suspicious grey moon.

seats.want: Climb into the space truck on the Riser and leave this dusty planet today, taking the tin-can robot with you if you can.
Breathe very loudly while you hunt for the tin-can robot, then grab it and march it to the Back, where your shuttle waits.
Teach anyone who will listen your ancient art of waving the glow-stick sword, then give it to your best student.
Guard your space truck on the Riser with the toy blaster, and let nobody aboard until they hand you something valuable up front.
Grab the toy blaster and keep the tin-can robot out of the wrong hands until you can give it to the one actor you trust.

cards.title: The Ring Is Mine, I Mean Ours
cards.premise: Deep in an old dwarf mine, a band of travelers must cross a narrow stone bridge before a big, grumpy fire monster who hates noise wakes up. The cursed gold ring they are hauling to a volcano tempts everyone who touches it. The Riser is the narrow bridge, and the monster snores at the Back.

backdrop.what: A huge old dwarf mine: carved stone pillars, a deep chasm with a thin stone bridge, and a warm orange glow rising from far below.

seats.want: Grab the cursed ring, cross the Riser bridge to Right, and talk anyone who gets hold of it into giving it back.
Grab the glowing staff, plant yourself on the Riser, and keep everyone off the bridge until you decide it is safe.
Get the cursed ring into your own hands for just a moment, from the Prop Table or from whoever has it, and swear you were only checking it for scratches.
Prove this old mine has the best echo anywhere by throwing the water bucket at Back as hard as you can.
Keep your hair perfect in the footlights at Front, and talk anyone holding the water bucket into handing it to you.

cards.title: Dino Island Is Mostly Safe
cards.premise: A billionaire cloned dinosaurs for an island theme park, and today is opening day. The fences just lost power, a dino egg rolled out of the hatchery, and the tour group is still out in the jungle. The Riser is the park's lookout tower.

backdrop.what: A steamy island jungle with a sagging electric fence, a tilted warning sign, giant muddy footprints and a smoking volcano far away.

seats.want: Carry the dino egg to every guest in turn and insist it proves the park is perfectly safe.
Get every guest up on the Riser before something big shows up, and scold anyone who climbs back down.

seats.role: A runaway dinosaur with tiny arms
seats.want: Get your dino egg back from wherever it ends up, and roar at anyone who touches it.
Feed the meaty drumstick to a dinosaur, or to whoever looks most like one, no matter what the grown-ups say.
Hand the safety waiver to every guest to sign, then hide at the Back far from anything with teeth.

cards.title: The Favor Father
cards.premise: The family boss's daughter is getting married in the garden. Tradition says nobody may say no to a favor on her wedding day, so every guest is asking for one. The Riser is the boss's big chair at the head table.

backdrop.what: A sunny garden wedding: a striped party tent, paper lanterns, lemon trees, a tiered cake and a pink stucco villa.

seats.role: The family boss, father of the bride
seats.want: Sit on the Riser like a king, say yes to every favor anyone asks, and seal each deal by handing over the cannoli tray.
Take offense at every tiny insult to the family, throw the cannoli tray at whoever said it, then storm off to sulk at the Back.
Stay out of the family business: hide at the Front by the footlights and dodge anyone who comes over to ask a favor, because today you cannot say no.
Fix every problem the same quiet way: grab the plush horse head and throw it at whoever is causing trouble.
Win a starring movie role: croon a sad song at the Front, then give the wedding envelope to whoever looks most in charge and beg for help.

cards.title: What's in the Glowing Briefcase?
cards.premise: A retro diner on dance-contest night, and everyone inside is up to something. A glowing briefcase that nobody may open sits on the Prop Table, which is the diner counter. The Riser is the dance-contest stage.

backdrop.what: A retro diner: a chrome counter with cherry-red stools, a checkered floor, plump booths, a big wall clock and wide windows onto a sunny parking lot.

seats.role: A chatty errand man in a black suit
seats.want: Carry the glowing briefcase to the boss's booth at the Back, chatting about burgers all the way, and let nobody open it.

seats.role: A nosy errand man in a black suit
seats.want: Get the glowing briefcase to yourself at the Front and peek inside it while nobody is looking.
Win the dance contest on the Riser, pull anyone you like up to be your partner, and claim the giant milkshake as your prize.

seats.role: A runaway boxer who refused to lose
seats.want: Grab your lucky gold pocket watch before anyone else can and keep it safe at Left, dodging anyone who asks about the big fight.

seats.role: A smooth fixer in a tuxedo
seats.want: Clean up the chaos in record time: grab any prop left lying loose and throw it back onto the Prop Table.

cards.title: League Night, Bathrobe Optional
cards.premise: League night at the neighborhood bowling alley, the night of the big semifinal. A slacker in a bathrobe has been mistaken for a millionaire with the same name, and now somebody has to drop off a ransom bag at the Back before the last frame. The Riser is the winners' podium.

backdrop.what: A retro bowling alley on league night: shiny wooden lanes, rows of white pins, a ball return and a starry ceiling.

seats.role: A laid-back slacker in a bathrobe
seats.want: Replace your ruined rug with the rolled-up rug, throw it down at Center, and stay relaxed no matter who yells at you.

seats.role: A hot-headed teammate who knows every rule
seats.want: Take charge of the ransom bag, throw it at the Back yourself, and call a foul on anyone who questions your plan.

seats.role: A quiet bowler nobody listens to
seats.want: Get the bowling ball and finally take your turn, rolling it at the pins at the Back, before anyone cuts you off.
Claim the Riser as your winners' podium before a single frame is bowled, and hold up the bowling ball like you already won.
Get the rolled-up rug back, since it was your mother's, and throw it onto the Riser as your newest work of art.

cards.title: Pick a Pill, Any Pill
cards.premise: Midnight in a gray office that is secretly a computer program. Someone here is about to be offered a red pill or a blue pill, agents in dark suits are closing in, and the ringing phone is the only way out. The Riser is the boss's big leather armchair.

backdrop.what: A gray office after midnight: rows of clay cubicles, one buzzing ceiling light, a rainy window and old computer screens dripping with green light.

seats.want: Refuse to choose: give away any pill or prop that reaches you, and keep sneaking back to the Riser for a nap.

seats.role: A grand leader in a long coat
seats.want: Grab a pill, settle into the Riser, and give it to whoever looks most confused, swishing your coat dramatically.
Grab the ringing phone and give it to whoever seems ready to escape, and dodge in slow motion at Center whenever anything is thrown.

seats.role: A stern agent in a dark suit
seats.want: Gather up every loose pill and the ringing phone, throw them back onto the Prop Table, and glare at any actor who looks suspiciously like a pill.
Stir your cookie dough at the Back, then give a pill to whoever you predict will pick the wrong one.

notes.riddle: Some corners of my stage are cursed.

notes.note: Move to Center in your first turn, then never move anywhere else.
notes.opposite: Never go to Center, and keep moving all scene.
notes.riddle: Find my spotlight early, then put down roots.
notes.autocorrect: Move to Center in your thirst turn, then never move anywhere elks.

notes.note: Grab a prop in your first turn and hold it all scene. Never throw it or give it away.
notes.opposite: Never hold a prop for long. Throw or give away anything you grab.
notes.riddle: Whatever you pick up first, love it forever.
notes.autocorrect: Grab a prawn in your first turn and hold it all seen. Never throw it or give it away.

notes.note: Grab a prop, then give it to another actor on your next turn.
notes.opposite: Grab a prop, then never let another actor have it.
notes.riddle: Take something, then make a gift of it.
notes.autocorrect: Crab a prop, then give it to another actor on your next tern.

notes.note: Throw something at least once, at the actor you trust least.
notes.opposite: Never throw anything at the actor you trust most.
notes.riddle: Your least favorite castmate deserves a flying gift.
notes.autocorrect: Throw something at lest once, at the actor you thrust least.

notes.note: Climb onto the Riser at least once.
notes.riddle: Every actor deserves one moment above the rest.
notes.autocorrect: Clime onto the Riser at yeast once.

notes.note: Move to a different place every turn.
notes.opposite: Stay in the same place every turn.
notes.riddle: A rolling robot gathers no suspicion.
notes.autocorrect: Moo to a different palace every turn.

notes.note: Start every turn by looking at another actor.
notes.opposite: Never look at another actor on any turn.
notes.riddle: Before you act, lock eyes with a castmate.
notes.autocorrect: Start every churn by looking at another factor.

notes.note: Mention your favorite prop every time you speak.
notes.opposite: Never mention any prop when you speak.
notes.riddle: Every line, gush about the prop you love most.
notes.autocorrect: Mention your favorite prom every thyme you speak.

notes.note: End every line with a question.
notes.opposite: End no line with a question.
notes.riddle: Why end a line any other way?
notes.autocorrect: Bend every lion with a question.
